technical-data.invention-title: WATER PURIFICATION ARRANGEMENT FOR DRAIN WATER CATCH BASINS
ENSEMBLE DE PURIFICATION DES EAUX DESTINE AUX BASSINS COLLECTEURS POUR EAUX USEES

abstract.p: An arrangement (2) for cleansing polluted water that enters into a catch basin includes a container (4), which is intended to be arranged in the catch basin and which has an upper, substantially horizontal intake opening (30) for receiving the downward moving polluted water, and a pollution-absorbing material (6) that is arranged in the container for cleansing polluted water that flows from the intake opening. The arrangement further includes a particle separator (8) which is arranged above the container (4) and which forms an outer surface (18) with a shape such that solid particles in the incoming, polluted water are diverted by the outer surface so that the particles fall outside of the intake opening (30) of the container, whereas water is led in under the particle separator (8) by surface wetting to the outer surface and falls down into the container via its intake opening.

L'invention concerne un ensemble (2) destiné à la purification des eaux polluées qui pénètrent dans un bassin collecteur. Cet ensemble comprend un récipient (4), destiné à être installé dans le bassin collecteur et possédant une ouverture d'entrée supérieure (30) sensiblement horizontale qui reçoit les eaux polluées s'écoulant vers l'aval, et un matériau (6) absorbant la pollution, aménagé dans le récipient et servant à purifier les eaux polluées qui s'écoule depuis l'ouverture d'entrée. L'ensemble comprend également un séparateur de particules (8) aménagé en dessus du récipient et formant une surface externe (18) dont la forme permet de dévier les particules solides contenues dans les eaux polluées qui arrivent et de les faire tomber en dehors de l'ouverture d'entrée (30) du récipient, l'eau étant amenée à l'intérieur sous le séparateur de particules (8) par l'humidification de la surface externe et pénétrant dans le récipient à travers l'ouverture d'entrée.

description.p: WATER PURIFICATION ARRANGEMENT FOR DRAIN WATER CATCH BASINS

The present invention relates to an arrangement for cleansing polluted water that enters into a drain water catch basin, comprising a container that is intended to be arranged m the catch basin and that has at least one upper, substantially horizontal intake opening to receive downward flowing, polluted water, and at least one lower outlet opening for evacuating the cleansed water from the container. A pollution-absorbing material is arranged m the container for cleansing the polluted water that flows from the intake opening to the outlet opening. Water purification arrangements of this type have been used foremost for primary purification of surface water, which often contains environmentally harmful pollutants in both solid and liquid form, such as heavy metals, rubber particles, oil and chemicals. Such pollutants put an unfavorable load on the purification plants and disrupt the intended function of the chemical and biological purification steps. In the case where the polluted water is not connected to a purification plant, the soil, ground water, and recipients are impacted m an unfavorable manner. When water purification arrangements of this type are installed m dram water catch basins for surface water, there is the advantage that the said pollutants can be separated from the surface water even before it reaches the purification plant. Additionally, separated pollutants in the form of oil residues and certain chemicals can advantageously be converted into environmentally friendly substances with the help of bacteria cultures m the pollution-absorbing material, for example, bark.

One problem m this context is, however, that solid particles such as gravel, trash, leaves and the like, which fall down into the dram water catch basin, can, in exposed positions, completely clog the intake opening of the arrangement's container relatively quickly, sometimes in
only a few weeks after installation of the water purification arrangement. Since, for reasons of cost, the arrangement cannot be cleaned or provided with a new pollution-absorbing material more often than approximately three times per year, there is therefore a risk that the arrangement m certain drain water catch basins will be useless a large part of the year.

Another problem is that the flow of water down into the drain water catch basin usually varies greatly. The water flow can therefore be significantly larger than the normal flow that the water purification arrangement is dimensioned to receive, which can lead to pollutants that have been absorbed by the pollution-absorbing material being purged out of it. Moreover, the water flow can sometimes be extremely much larger tnan the said normal flow, which can lead to flooding due to the arrangement reducing the flow capacity of the drain water catch basin.
The goal of the present invention is to provide an improved water purification arrangement that solves the above-mentioned problems found m water purification arrangements of this specific type.

This goal is achieved by means of an arrangement of the type described m the introduction which is characterized by including a particle separator, which is arranged above the container and that forms an outer surface having such a shape that solid particles m the incoming cleansed water are diverted by the outer wall so that the particles fall outside of the intake opening, whereas water is led due to surface wetting m under the particle separator and falls down into the container via its intake opening. In this way, clogging of the intake opening of the container by coarse, solid particles m a form of trash, branches, larger leaves and the like, which fall down into the dram water catch basin, is efficiently avoided. Thanks to the surface wetting of the water on the outer surface of the container, an incoming normal flow of polluted water can be lead under the container where the water is collected, so that it ultimately releases from the
outer surface and falls down through tne intake opening of the container.

The outer surface of the particle separator advantageously extends horizontally, seen from above, and covers the horizontal intake opening of the container, which has the effect that an extremely large incoming flow of water, which is substantially not influenced by the surface wetting on the outer surface, for the most part falls outside the intake opening of the container. In this way, the particle separator acts as a flow regulator the sense that only a predetermined maximum water flow can flow into the container, regardless of how large the flow of water is that enters the dra water catch basin. The arrangement thus avoids pollutants that have been absorbed by the pollution-absorning material m the container being flushed out of it during abnormally large incoming flows of water. The risk of flooding is also reduced, since large flows of water can pass outside of the container the dra water catch basin. According to one general aspect of the invention, at least a part of the outer service of the particle separator is curved, preferably from the top of the particle separator downward and m under the particle separator, which has the result that the normal flow of water can easily flow along the curved outer surface due to surface wetting, with no risk of the water releasing from the outer service .

According to one embodiment of the invention, the outer surface of the particle separator is substantially cylindrical, which makes the particle separator simple and economical to manufacture. The cylindrical outer surface may suitably be delimited by two end flanges on the particle separator, in order to prevent incoming water from running off of the outer surface of the cylinder at its end walls.

Figure 3 shows a perspective view of the rear portion of the embodiment according to Figure 1; Figure 4 shows a view obliquely from above of the front portion of the embodiment according to Figure 1 ;
Figure 5 shows a side view of the embodiment according to Figure 1 with a cover removed;
Figure 6 shows another embodiment of the arrangement according to the invention;
Figure 7 shows a funnel m the arrangement according to the invention for receiving and distributing polluted water;
Figure 8 shows a view from above of the funnel according to Figure 7 ;
Figure 9 schematically illustrates how the funnel can be attached to different sizes of intake grates for dram water catch basms.

Figure 1 shows an arrangement 2 according to one embodiment of the invention that includes two mam parts, namely, a container 4 for a pollution-absorbing material 6, for example, bark, and a particle separator 8 that is arranged above the container 4. The particle separator 8 comprises a cylindrical wall 10 and two end walls 12, 14, whereby the walls 10, 12 and 14 delimit a chamber 16. The cylindrical wall 10 has a cylindrical outer surface 18 that is axially delimited by two flanges 20, 22, which form radial extensions of the end walls 12, 14. Located centrally m the lower part of the particle separator 8 there is a vertical passage 24 m the wall 10. The end walls 12, 14 each have an oval hole 26 and 28, respectively, whereby the one hole 26 extends below the lower limit of the second hole 28.

The container 4 forms a ring-shaped flange 28, which delimits a horizontal upper intake opening 30, under which is arranged a removable, fine strainer 32. A fine strainer 36, which supports the pollution-absorbing material 6, is arranged on the container 4 and extends above a lower outlet opening 34 of the container. Two side walls 38, 40
of the container 4 transition seamlessly into the end wails 12, 14 of the particle separator 8, whereby the particle separator 8 and the container 4 form a single unit. Located between the side walls 38, 40 of the container 4 is a removable cover 42, which covers a side opening 44 into the interior of the container 4 (see Figure 5) .

On either side of the particle separator 8 is formed a passage 46 and 48, respectively, between the container 4 and the respective portions 50, 52 of the cylindrical outer surface 18 that curves inwards under the particle separator 8. Positioned m the passages 46, 48 are coarse strainers 54 , 56, respectively, m the form of grates, which extend downward from the outer surface 18 towards the container 4.

Figure 6 shows schematically an alternative embodiment of the invention, m which the particle separator 58 is shaped to have a spherical outer surface 60; the container 62 for the pollution-absorbing material is cylindrical; and the coarse strainer 64 in the passage between the spherical outer surface 60 and the container 4 is ring-shaped. At its lower end the cylindrical container 62 is provided with a grate 66.

In Figures 7 and 8 is shown an elastic funnel 68, for example, made of rubber, with a square cross section. The funnel 68 is provided with fastening members 70, which are intended to be attached to suitable fastening members 72 on the upper part of the particle separator 8. (The funnel 68 can naturally also be attached to the particle separator 58 as shown m Figure 6 by means of suitable fasteners.) The funnel 68 is intended to be fastened onto existing square intake grates 74, 76 of different sizes by cutting the funnel 68 so that it fits the current intake grate, as is indicated m Figure 9. In this way, the entire arrangement according to the invention, including the funnel 68, will hang from the intake grate 74, 76 down into the dram water catch basin. Alternatively, the funnel 68 may be shaped to have a circular cross-section m order to fit any circular intake grates.
The arrangement according to the invention works m the following way, with reference to the embodiment according to Figures 1 - 5. Aided by the funnel 68, the arrangement 2 is attached to the intake grate 74, 76 to the dram water catch basin which the incoming, polluted surface water is to be cleansed. The intake grate 74, 76 is then put on the dram water catch basin so that the arrangement 2 hangs down into it. Polluted water that has a flow of normal size down through the intake grate 74, 76 is collected by the funnel 68 and is distributed centrally onto the upper part of the cylindrical outer surface 18 of the particle separator 8. The water flows farther down following the cylindrical outer surface 18 and, by surface wetting on the parts 50 and 52, into the passages 46 and 48 through the coarse strainers 54 and 56 The flanges 20 and 22 then hinder the water from running onto the end walls 12 and 14. Solid, heavy particles m the incoming surface water fall away from the cylindrical outer surface 18 outside of the passages 46 and 56, down onto the bottom of the catch basin, whereas solid, relatively large, light particles, which are carried along by the water into the passages 46 and 48, are separated by the coarse strainers 54 and 56. Water that has passed the coarse strainers 54 and 56 separates from the parts 50 and 52 of the cylindrical outer surface 18 at the passage 24 and falls down through the intake opening 30 of the container 4, through the fine strainer 32, which separates any solid, relatively small, light particles. The absorbing material 6 absorbs any oil or chemical residues the water passing it. Finally, the cleansed water flows out from the container 4 via the fine strainer 36 and into the outlet opening 34.

If the flow of the surface water through the intake grate 74, 76 is greater than the normal flow that the arrangement 2 is dimensioned to receive, then the excess water will release from the cylindrical outer surface 18 of the particle separator 8 and will fall down outside of the passages 46 and 48. A maximum water flow will flow through the passages 46 and 48 and fill the container 4 above the
absorbing material 6, since this material does not have the capacity to receive such a maximum flow. As a result, the water above the absorbing material 6 will rise up through the lower vertical passage 24 in the cylindrical wall 10 and will flow out from the chamber of the particle separator 8 via the lower hole 26, whereby solid, relatively small, light particles are carried from the fine strainer 32 by the flowing water that is flowing on it. The fine strainer 32 is thus flushed automatically during those instances when the flow of the surface water is greater than normal .

The arrangement according to the invention has been described above in the context of installing the arrangement in a drain water catch basin for surface water. It can, however, alternatively be used in other applications where one wishes to purify flowing, polluted water. The expression "drain water catch basin" should therefore be interpreted broadly and to comprise equivalent elements that form a space for a substantially vertically flowing stream of water, for example, wells in laundry facilities, industrial catch basins, rain gutters from roofs, and the like.

claim.claim-text: 1. An arrangement (2) for cleansing polluted water that enters into a catch basin, comprising a container (4; 62), which is intended to be arranged in the catch basin and which has at least one upper, substantially horizontal intake opening (30) for receiving the downward moving polluted water, and at least one lower outlet opening (34) for evacuating cleansed water from the container, and a pollution-absorbing material (6) that is arranged in the container for cleansing polluted water that flows from the intake opening to the outlet opening, characterized by comprising a particle separator (8; 58) which is arranged above the container (4; 62) and that forms an outer surface (18; 60) with a shape such that solid particles in the incoming, polluted water are diverted by the outer surface so that the particles fall outside of the intake opening (30) of the container, whereas water is led in under the particle separator by surface wetting to the outer surface and falls down into the container via its intake opening.

2. An arrangement according to claim 1, characterized by the outer surface (18; 60) of the particle separator (8; 58) having a horizontal extension, which, seen from above, covers the horizontal intake opening (30) of the container (4) .
3. An arrangement according to claim 2, characterized by at least one part of the outer surface (18; 60) of the particle separator (8; 58) being curved.
4. An arrangement according to claim 3, characterized by the outer surface (18; 60) of the particle separator (8; 58) curving downward and in under the particle separator.

5. An arrangement according to claim 4, characterized by the outer surface (18; 60) of the particle separator (8; 58) curving from the top of the particle separator downward and in under the particle separator.
6. An arrangement according to claim 5, characterized by the outer surface (18) of the particle separator (8) being substantially cylindrical.

7. An arrangement according to claim 6, characterized by the cylindrical outer surface (18) being delimited by two end flanges (20, 22) on the particle separator (8) . 8. An arrangement according to claim 5, characterized by the outer surface (60) of the particle separator (58) being substantially spherical.

9. An arrangement according to any of the claims 4-8, characterized in that at least one passage (46, 48) for polluted water is formed between the container (4; 62) and the part of the outer surface (18; 60) of the particle separator (8; 58) that curves in under the particle separator, and in that a relatively coarse strainer (54, 56; 64) for separating relatively large, light particles from the cleansed water is arranged in said passage .

10. An arrangement according to any of the claims 1-9, characterized by comprising a funnel (68) for receiving polluted water and distributing the received water centrally above and onto the particle separator
(8; 58) whereby the funnel is arranged to be fastened onto an existing intake grate (74, 76) of a drain water catch basin, in which the arrangement is to be located.
